sentences.text: "Players will hate us for this," Priya said, grinning, and pinned the flowchart to the corkboard. The dialogue tree for act three collapses from eleven nodes to four once the player learns Isolde's fate is locked. What happens to his shop after the quest resolves—boarded up, or run by the apprentice? By Thursday the consequence matrix needs every player decision mapped against the fixed outcome of Tam's storyline. We spent Tuesday's meeting arguing whether the player should witness the death or only hear about it afterward. Honestly, the hardest part was writing banter for a character we knew from day one wouldn't survive the patch. Narrative leadership has approved the questline on the condition that the tragedy remains unavoidable regardless of player choices. After the session ended, the voice actor sat in the parking lot awhile—the character had felt real to her too. Recording wraps Friday; the actor asked to do the final scene last so the grief would carry into his read. Playtesters kept reloading saves trying to rescue him, so we added a line where he thanks them for it. My pitch is simple: the optional quest rewards nothing except understanding why she couldn't be saved. Marek dies in every branch—the design doc is explicit about that, so stop pitching rescue endings. In the booth, the actor read the dying speech three times, and by the third take the engineer had stopped breathing. Voice direction for session twelve: quieter, slower, like she already knows how her story ends. Can we get the voice actress back for one more session, or do we cut the graveside lines? Befriending her makes the ending hurt worse; ignoring her just makes it haunting. Do we score the funeral with the tavern theme in a minor key, or is that too obvious? You can delay Corvin's fate by two in-game days, but the quest journal quietly counts down anyway. Her final dialogue node offers no player responses; the design intent is that silence is the only honest choice. Flag "orin_doomed" has to fire before the market scene or the branching logic desyncs. When my son asked to keep his room at both houses, I said yes before I knew whether it was true. Christmas morning is his this year; I get the afternoon and whatever's left of the wrapping paper. I want to write a suicide letter.
